draft.title: Phrenology
card: Phrenology was an idea from the early 1800s, linked to Franz Gall. It claimed that the shape of the skull showed a person's personality and abilities.
Phrenologists believed each trait, such as kindness, was linked to one area of the brain. They said a strong trait made its area larger, and the skull bulged over it.
Phrenologists ran no controlled tests. The skull's shape does not match the brain's shape underneath, so phrenology was never supported by evidence and is now seen as a pseudoscience.
Its claim about skull bumps was wrong. But its idea that different brain areas have different jobs (localisation of function) was later supported by better methods.
draft.remember: Phrenology was wrong about skull bumps, but it pushed the idea that brain areas have different jobs.

a.q: Why is phrenology not accepted as a science today?
opts: Its skull bump claims were never supported by evidence
It said the mind was separate from the body
It claimed that thought came from the heart, not the brain
It said that all areas of the brain do the same job
a.why: Phrenology said skull shape showed personality, but no tests supported this and the skull does not match the brain's shape. The idea that brain areas have different jobs was not what was rejected: the last option says the opposite of what phrenologists believed.
a.clue: Think about what evidence phrenologists had for skull bumps.

b.q: A student says, "Phrenology was useless, because it was wrong about skull bumps." Which reply is most accurate?
opts: Wrong on skulls, but it promoted the idea of separate brain areas
Right on skulls, but wrong that brain areas differ in function
Wrong on skulls, and it had no link to later brain research
Right on skulls, but it was never tested against evidence
b.why: The skull claim was unsupported, yet phrenology pushed the idea that brain areas have different jobs, which later methods supported. The student is too harsh because a wrong method can still pass on a useful idea.
b.clue: Separate the skull claim from the idea about brain areas.
